summary: Module 6 CONTEXT micro-exercise: map three system boundaries in the fork and the assumptions at each. Boundary 1 -- API -> Redis cache (redirect path): routers/redirect.py reads redirect targets from cache via services/cache.py, and writes/invalidates on update. Assumption: 'the cache entry I read is current, not stale'. This was silently believed until my M3 fix made it ENFORCED via a version token (INCR on invalidate, WATCH/MULTI conditional populate, reject version-mismatch on read). Boundary 2 -- API -> Celery broker (click recording): redirect.py enqueues record_click jobs onto the 'click_events' queue in Redis; the Celery worker consumes and calls insert_click. Assumption: 'the broker has the message and a worker will process it'. This is fire-and-forget .delay() -- NOT enforced anywhere (no DLQ, no ack monitoring, no consumer heartbeat); if the broker evicts or the worker is down, clicks are silently lost, and the idempotent event_key only protects against duplicates, not loss. Boundary 3 -- Celery worker -> Postgres (and shared with API): the worker opens its own SessionLocal() to insert clicks, sharing the same pool as the API. Assumption: 'a pooled connection is always available'. Not enforced -- connection pool exhaustion in the API (long-held sessions) silently chokes the worker's inserts and vice versa, the classic cascading failure the module describes. Documented-elsewhere assumptions: ratelimit.py InMemoryStorage assumes single-process deployment (comment-documented, NOT enforced) -- under Celery multi-worker the rate limit silently becomes per-process instead of global. Each boundary is a place where the system 'works' in isolation but the contract between the parts is only believed, not verified -- exactly the multi-layer-bug terrain of this module.
evidence: Boundary 1 (cache->DB): version token now enforces the currentness contract
Boundary 2 (API->queue): fire-and-forget .delay(), no DLQ/heartbeat, event_key idempotency only covers duplicates
Boundary 3 (worker->DB): shared SessionLocal pool; pool exhaustion cascades between API and worker
ratelimit.py: single-process assumption documented in comment, not enforced
